title: Allow rules: matcher, store, routes, answerer
what:
src/allow/ implements watch::Sink. It binds DoorKey -> chat id through sessions::id_of_pid when it first needs it.
matcher.rs is pure: fn(rules, ask, door) -> Option<rid>. A rule matches only when all hold:
- kind == approval; questions are never answered
- the chat mode is auto or manual
- the ask was first seen after the rule was created
- ask.origin is Some and equals rule.origin. A rule made on a model call never answers a script's nested call via tool_call (host.rs:1364-1377); unknown origin never matches.
- the tool name is byte-exact
- for bash: input.command is a String equal to rule.command byte for byte after JSON decode (a trailing space, CRLF or a lookalike fails); input.background is absent or false (a 'true' string also fails); timeout_s is ignored; the door's hello cwd equals rule.cwd
- for any other tool: ask.structural == false
store.rs, per D10:
- (a) memory only, each rule bound to the door pid alive when it was made: any stop, model or mode switch, or perch restart ends it
- (b) <home>/allow.json, 0600, cleared when the mode recorded at creation differs from the current one
- at most 32 rules per chat
Routes:
- GET /hub/sessions/<id>/allow -> {mode, rules:[{rid, tool, origin, command?, cwd?, added_ms, uses, last_ms?}]}
- POST /hub/sessions/<id>/allow {ask_id}
  - the rule is built from the watcher's own copy of that ask (tool, input, origin); nothing is read from the body but ask_id
  - the perch answers that ask yes itself
  - 201 {rule, answered:'yes'|'lost'}
  - 409: not pending, not an approval, yolo, or the cap
  - 422: a structural ask with a name rule, a background bash call, or an ask whose origin is unknown
- POST /hub/sessions/<id>/revoke {rid} -> 204 | 404
Answerer: a spawned POST to the door's /api/answer {ask_id, answer:'yes', note: RULE_NOTE}.
- RULE_NOTE = "allowed by the operator's rule for this chat (Minerva)" (ASCII, ≤ 1024 bytes).
- It selects on ctx.stop, so shutdown never waits on it.
- 204 means done; 409 means the page won, ignore it.
tests:
Pure matcher unit tests for every clause. No match on:
- a trailing space or a different cwd
- background:true or 'true'
- a question
- yolo
- a structural name rule
- an ask pending before the rule
- a skipped long line
- a script-origin ask with the same command as a model-origin rule
- an ask with unknown origin
tests/allow.rs with fake_eidolon FAKE_ASKS:
- allow, then a second identical model-origin ask is answered with the note in the body
- revoke stops it
- a mode switch (restart) clears; a fork has none
- a page-first answer (409) is ignored
- after a lagged reconnect, replayed asks are not double-answered
- a body carrying tool, command or origin fields cannot shape the rule
- perch SIGTERM with an answer in flight exits in under 3 s
- (D10 b) allow.json is 0600 and a corrupt one is set aside
live_check: fake perch on PORT=48122 + curl: the scripted ask is auto-settled and the fake's answer log shows RULE_NOTE.
risk:
- An exact command is not an exact effect: ./build.sh or cargo test run files the model can edit.
- A user tool registered under the name bash and called by the model has the same name and origin, so it inherits bash rules.
- The model sees RULE_NOTE.
All go to XS.
